title: POC scoping - Data handling & logging (Arcadia Health)
summary: POC scope focused on data handling: PII redaction, logging/retention settings, prompt storage concerns. Agreement to run a 2-week benchmark on dedicated capacity with redaction layer, measure latency/cost, and provide security pack + integration guide.
next_steps: Redwood to send security pack and SOC2 docs (Sophie) by 2026-08-22
Customer to share sample anonymized dataset and typical request profile (Luis) by 2026-08-25
Schedule 2-week dedicated benchmark window late Aug / early Sep (Daniel & Tom)
action_items: Sophie Martin: Send security pack + architecture diagram (due 2026-08-22)
Luis Ramirez: Provide sample request logs and token distribution (due 2026-08-25)
Daniel Cho: Prepare benchmark plan & cost estimate for 2-week Dedicated run (due 2026-08-24)
Tom Ye: Confirm networking/VPC peering constraints and egress policy (due 2026-08-23)
transcript:
[00:00] Sophie Martin: Hi everyone, thanks for joining, this is Sophie from Redwood, with Daniel our solutions engineer and Maya on CSM.
[00:07] Priya Nair: Hi, thanks. Quick introductions - I'm Priya, CTO at Arcadia. We're here to scope the POC around handling patient data for our chatbot.
[00:15] Sophie Martin: Great. High level we want to understand success criteria, what data flows look like, and what benchmarks you need.
[00:23] Luis Ramirez: Primary concerns are PII leakage in logs, prompt storage, and retention. We also need latency targets our SLAs are 200ms p50 for short queries.
[00:35] Daniel Cho: Okay. For the POC we typically suggest a dedicated capacity run so you can measure throughput and latency deterministically. We can enable a redaction pre-processor to strip PHI before it hits the model.
[00:47] Karen Holt: Can you talk about what "redaction" actually means in your flow? Are you storing original prompts anywhere?
[00:54] Daniel Cho: Good question. Default hosted logs keep request/response payloads for troubleshooting but we can offer options: full retention, redacted-only retention, or no storage. For Enterprise/private we support turning off request body logging and only keeping telemetry.
[01:08] Sophie Martin: To add, we have a configurable retention policy per route; you can set zero retention for prompt bodies and keep only aggregated metrics. We also offer automatic redaction rules - regex and ML-based entity detection. It's not perfect \u2014 there are false negatives \u2014 so we recommend a short redaction review step.
[01:28] Priya Nair: How about prompt embedding storage? We compute embeddings to power rerankers and sometimes we cache prompts. Is that stored raw?
[01:35] Daniel Cho: Embeddings by default are ephemeral unless you opt into using Redwood Optimize features that persist them for vector search. For the POC we can keep everything ephemeral, or persist hashed references only.
[01:47] Tom Ye: From infra side, we need to know networking. Would this POC run in our VPC or on Redwood dedicated infrastructure? We need to ensure egress rules and data residency.
[01:58] Sophie Martin: Two options: Redwood Dedicated in a shared Redwood account (isolated GPU pools) or Private deployment with VPC peering. For a quick POC we usually spin up a dedicated pool in region and set up TLS + customer-managed KMS for keys. For strict data residency we can do Private.
[02:14] Priya Nair: SOC2 and encryption at rest \u2014 do you support customer-managed KMS or HSM?
[02:19] Daniel Cho: Yes, we support KMS integration (AWS KMS / GCP KMS) and HSM via our Private offering. We can also provide audit logs on key usage.
[02:27] Karen Holt: Is the redaction done client-side or server-side? We prefer client-side before sending any PHI to Redwood.
[02:33] Sophie Martin: You can do client-side redaction and use our server-side as a safety net. For the POC we recommend both: client-side deterministic scrubbing (e.g., mask MRNs, SSNs) plus server-side NER-based redaction so any slips are caught.
[02:48] Luis Ramirez: If we client-redact, we still want to send a hashed id so we can correlate across requests. Concern is hashing salt and reversibility.
[02:55] Daniel Cho: We recommend HMAC with customer-managed salt. We do not store salts. If you need reversible mapping you should manage that in your infra.
[03:05] Priya Nair: Benchmarks \u2014 what do you typically measure in a 2-week run?
[03:10] Daniel Cho: Latency percentiles (p50/p95/p99), throughput (reqs/sec), cost per 1K tokens, and model accuracy metrics based on your eval prompts. We'll also measure cold vs warmed KV cache performance.
[03:22] Sophie Martin: We'll instrument end-to-end including network hop time; Daniel will share the benchmark plan. Expect synthetic load + a replay of your sample logs to approximate production distribution.
[03:33] Luis Ramirez: We'll provide token distribution and a 2000-record sample set; but note many prompts contain PHI \u2014 we'll provide anonymized versions and a small human-reviewed PHI set for leakage testing.
[03:44] Karen Holt: For leakage testing we need proof that original prompt data is not stored and an audit trail showing deletion. What's the retention delete process?
[03:52] Daniel Cho: We have per-route retention settings. Delete requests are audited; for hosted we purge within retention windows and provide a deletion confirmation. For Private, you control storage and deletion. We'll include retention API details in the security pack.
[04:06] Tom Ye: What about prompt telemetry \u2014 conversation ids, user ids? Are those stored in plain?
[04:11] Sophie Martin: Those are configurable. You can hash IDs client-side and send hashed values. Redwood can drop PII fields before logging. We also support differential telemetry where only aggregate metrics are kept.
[04:23] Priya Nair: Success criteria for the POC: 1) No measurable PII leakage in the test set, 2) Latency p95 under 450ms for the expected load, 3) Cost projection within our budget target.
[04:34] Sophie Martin: Sounds good. We'll formalize success criteria in the SOW. For the latency target, p50 200ms is tough on some models; p95 450ms is doable on Dedicated depending on sequence length and batching.
[04:48] Luis Ramirez: Can you give an example of where the latency tradeoff shows up? Like batching and cost?
[04:54] Daniel Cho: Sure. If you enable aggressive batching you'll improve throughput and lower cost per token but you increase tail latency. For interactive chat we suggest smaller batch windows and prefix caching to keep p95 down.
[05:06] Priya Nair: About logs \u2014 we need to ensure legal/forensic access in case of incident but without exposing PHI. Could logs be redacted and then sealed for forensics with access controls?
[05:16] Sophie Martin: Yes \u2014 we can store redacted logs in S3 with stricter ACLs and provide a secure access workflow for forensic requests. For sensitive artifacts we also support temporary access tokens and audit trails.
[05:28] Karen Holt: Anything to note about prompt templates and prompt storage in Redwood's tracing tools? We use templates that sometimes embed patient-specific fields.
[05:35] Daniel Cho: Tracing tools often capture the resolved prompt. We can instead capture template id and parameter hashes so you don't persist actual PHI. We'll show that configuration in the demo.
[05:45] Tom Ye: Network egress \u2014 will any data be routed through third-party services during the POC?
[05:50] Daniel Cho: No third-party telemetry by default. We only hit provider APIs for model hosting. For Private deployments you control the network. For Dedicated we can restrict egress to approved endpoints.
[06:00] Priya Nair: Timeline \u2014 we want a 2-week run starting as soon as we validate networking. Can we aim for Aug 31 start?
[06:07] Sophie Martin: Yes, that's feasible. Action items: we'll send security pack and a detailed POC plan by Aug 22. If you provide logs by Aug 25 we can start setup the week of Aug 26 and aim for Aug 31 run.
[06:20] Luis Ramirez: Will you provide cost estimates for the Dedicated run? We need to include it in our budget approval.
[06:25] Daniel Cho: We'll include a conservative cost estimate and a breakdown (GPU hours, storage, data transfer). Expect an optimized quantized model option versus a higher accuracy variant.
[06:35] Priya Nair: One more question \u2014 what about downstream data used for training models? We must ensure no training on customer data.
[06:41] Sophie Martin: Redwood does not use customer prompt/response data to train public models. For hosted we have an explicit flag to opt out of any data usage. Private obviously stays with you. We'll include the data usage policy in the docs.
[06:53] Karen Holt: Please include a sample DPA clause for retention and deletion.
[06:57] Sophie Martin: Will do.
[07:00] Maya Patel: Recap of next steps and owners: Sophie send security pack, Daniel bench plan, Luis sample data, Tom network details.
[07:10] Priya Nair: Thanks everyone, this was useful.
[07:12] Sophie Martin: Thanks, we'll follow up with a calendar invite for the kickoff.
[07:15] (call ends)

Notes: occasional transcription quirks: "Redwood Dediated" showed up in earlier slide share transcription, participant interrupts and overlapping talk noted. References: security pack (link shared), benchmark spreadsheet (drive link), SOW template.
